standard.title: Tone-syllables, intonation and phrasing for fluency
standard.description: use tone-syllables and apply intonation, stress and phrasing to develop fluency, and respond to and create texts in a range of contexts
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can use tonal features, intonation and stress to express feelings and opinions, apply tone change patterns, and use digital tools for fluency development (AC9LCH6U01). They have self-monitored spoken production. They have not yet developed comprehension of unfamiliar voices at varied speeds, analysed subtle regional accent differences, or applied fluency skills across a full range of text creation and response contexts.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students use tone-syllables, intonation, stress and phrasing to develop fluency in responding to and creating texts across a range of contexts — including comprehension of diverse speakers and speeds, and awareness of regional accent variation.

nodes.label: Auditory comprehension across diverse speakers
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can understand spoken target language from unfamiliar voices at varied speeds and levels of clarity, identifying key meaning and distinguishing subtle pronunciation variations.
nodes.minimum_width: Demonstrate comprehension of at least two spoken texts from unfamiliar voices at different speeds, identifying key information from each.
nodes.typical_width: Listen to short interactions between unfamiliar voices at diverse speeds and clarity levels; develop auditory comprehension strategies; distinguish subtle pronunciation differences including regional accents; compare own speech patterns with target language models and make adjustments.
wider: Listen to spoken target language from speakers across different regions and describe specific phonological differences heard — connect these to the regional dialect knowledge developed earlier
Compare comprehension strategies for fast native-speed speech with slower learner-directed speech — identify what makes fast speech harder to process and what strategies help
nodes.hinge_reason: Comprehension of diverse, unfamiliar speakers is the prerequisite for real-world spoken language use. Students who can only understand teacher-directed or familiar speech cannot function in authentic target language listening contexts — which is the threshold the Y7-8 curriculum marks.

response_modes.reason: Auditory comprehension across diverse speakers is built through repeated, varied listening exposure — different voices, speeds, accents, topics. A single familiar speaker type produces narrow comprehension that fails to generalise. Varied listening tasks build the flexible processing capacity needed.

success_criteria: Demonstrates comprehension of spoken target language from at least two unfamiliar voices
Identifies key information from at least one fast or less clearly articulated spoken text

nodes.label: Subtle tonal and pronunciation discrimination
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can discriminate subtle tonal and pronunciation differences — including tone change patterns and regional accent variation — and apply this awareness to their own spoken production.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two subtle pronunciation differences (tonal or segmental) between own speech and a target language model, and demonstrate an improvement attempt.
nodes.typical_width: Develop tone discrimination for subtle differences; distinguish between regional accent features; identify and practise tone change patterns including sandhi; compare own speech with models and make targeted adjustments; practise saying the same sentence to change meaning through tonal variation.
wider: Conduct a systematic comparison of own recorded speech with a native speaker model — identify and categorise specific pronunciation differences and design a targeted practice plan
Investigate a specific regional accent feature of the target language — describe the phonological rule, find examples, and compare with the standard form

response_modes.reason: Subtle tonal and pronunciation discrimination requires sustained, focused practice — these distinctions are not acquired through general exposure alone. Targeted self-monitoring activities with specific pronunciation goals build the perceptual and productive accuracy the descriptor requires.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Background learners have developed spoken habits that may differ systematically from standard target language pronunciation. Width investment in systematic self-comparison and targeted practice enables students to understand and control their own pronunciation — a metalinguistic awareness that is distinct from general fluency.
success_criteria: Identifies at least two subtle pronunciation differences between own speech and a model
Demonstrates a targeted improvement attempt for at least one identified difference

nodes.label: Fluency in text response and creation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can apply tonal and prosodic knowledge fluently when responding to and creating spoken texts across a range of contexts.
nodes.minimum_width: Respond to at least one spoken text and create at least one spoken text demonstrating fluency — appropriate phrasing, stress, tone and intonation — with minimal hesitation.
nodes.typical_width: Apply fluency skills across text response and creation contexts — discussions, presentations, performances, online interactions; use phrasing, grouping and intonation to support comprehension for listeners; create spoken texts that demonstrate tonal and prosodic control.
wider: Present a spoken text designed for a specific audience — demonstrate deliberate prosodic choices (pace, stress, pausing) that serve the communicative purpose
Record and review a full spoken performance across response and creation tasks — identify specific prosodic features that contribute to fluency and explain the choices made

response_modes.reason: Fluency in text contexts integrates auditory comprehension (node 1) and discrimination skills (node 2) into full spoken performance. The teaching investment is in creating genuine communicative conditions — real audiences, real response tasks — where fluency serves a communicative purpose.

success_criteria: Responds to a spoken text demonstrating comprehension through appropriate spoken or written reply
Creates a spoken text demonstrating fluency — appropriate phrasing, stress and intonation with minimal hesitation
